kill_reason: The assortment gap is ~zero and the research corpus's own diff already says so — it returns 46 of 46 lines "covered", ZERO "missing". I re-tested every line against the live catalogue anyway, because 17 of those 46 rested on junk evidence: the single word "amul" (638 SKUs, mostly chiller dairy) was the stated proof for SIX different lines (premium 70%+ dark, chocolate spread, ice cream cups, kulfi, family tubs, multipacks); "fruit" proved lollipops AND bubble gum; "candy" proved churan/goli, marshmallow, candy-toy AND ice pops. Re-probed properly, 44 of 46 lines are listed AND selling. Only 2 near-absences survive, both worth ~nothing: marshmallow/candy floss (1 match, a plastic basket named "Mellow") and ice cream cakes (4 birthday-cake SKUs in Pastrie, all dead since 2024, blocked by cold chain anyway). What is actually wrong is availability: 861 of 1,292 listed confectionery SKUs (66.6%) sold NOTHING in 12 months, 278 of the 431 that did sell are at zero-or-negative Stock.Quantity today, and only 6 SKUs of 431 sold in all 12 months. Adding SKUs to this category would make it worse.
penetration_assumption: The Rs 2,54,675 is NOT new demand — it is Rs 2,43,834 of recovered stock-outs plus Rs 10,840 of one restock. It is a floor, not a forecast. Method for the Rs 2,43,834: take only the 53 SKUs with PROVEN demand (sold in >=6 of the 12 months), find each SKU's own selling span (first to last selling month), count the months INSIDE that span where it sold nothing, and value each hole at that SKU's own MEDIAN monthly sales. Median not mean, so one festival month cannot inflate it. Using each SKU's own span rather than a fixed calendar is what makes this seasonality-safe automatically: a summer-only kulfi's winter absence falls outside its span and scores zero, as does a winter-only gazzak's summer absence. Assumption being made: a hole inside a proven SKU's own selling season is a stock-out, and the same median demand would have been captured had it been on the shelf. I deliberately did NOT extrapolate the 152 SKUs that sold 2-3 months or the 108 that sold exactly 1 month — extrapolating those to 12 months yields Rs 52 lakh, which is exactly the fantasy arithmetic that got the fleet to Rs 13.3 crore. The Rs 10,840 is Skippi Ice Pops 10/- and 20/-, which actually earned Rs 10,840 in the single summer (May-Aug 2024) they were stocked and have never been reordered — a proven number, not an assumption. Margins are VERIFIED per subgroup from the purchase ledger (PurchaseCost x sold qty vs FinalSaleAmount), not a blanket rate: Chocolate 18.32%, Ice Cream 27.08%, Toffee 28.15%, Sweets 16.08%, Gazzak 22.61%, Chewingum 19.27%, Aam Papad 43.06%. Blended 22.09% across 397 SKUs carrying both a purchase and a sale record. Uncertainty: the rupee figure could be off ~2x either way; the VERDICT is what I hold at high confidence.
probe_evidence:
All figures VERIFIED on a live 12-month window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 (feed live to 2026-08-30; the audit freeze is over). Scope = ARY's own subgroups Chocolate, Ice Cream, Ice Creams, Toffee, Chewingum, Sweets, Aam Papad, Milky Bar, Gazzak — NOT the group tag "Confectionery" (113), which also holds 831 biscuits, 682 snacks, 41 kurkure, 26 curd and 22 butter/cheese.

CATEGORY BASELINE (VERIFIED): 1,292 SKUs listed, 431 sold, 861 dead (66.6%), Rs 41,11,690. Prior 12m Rs 35,70,395 = +15.2% YoY. The category is GROWING.
CONTINUITY (VERIFIED): 6 SKUs sold in all 12 months; 24 in 10+; 108 in exactly 1; 260 of 431 in <=3 months.
STOCK NOW (VERIFIED, Stock.Quantity not the dead QuantityOnHand): 278 of 431 selling SKUs at zero-or-negative on-hand, carrying Rs 15,67,784 of the year's sales; their mean continuity is 2.83 months of 12 vs 5.00 for in-stock SKUs.

I WAS WRONG ONCE AND CAUGHT IT — this is Trap 2 replaying on me. My first chikki/gajak probe returned ZERO matches and I nearly reported "winter jaggery confectionery is genuinely absent". Wrong. ARY has a whole subgroup spelled "Gazzak": 25 SKUs, 12 selling, Rs 1,33,160 — Mahalakshmi Gazzak 200/300/400g, Mangatrai, Sunil Rewari, Marunda, Luxmi Gud Chana. My terms were gajak/revdi/chikki; ARY spells it gazzak/gajjak/rewari. Real ARY SKU names beat researcher vocabulary every time.

SECOND FALSE ALARM CAUGHT: the dead SKUs look like Rs 9,82,255 of prior-year revenue gone to zero, which reads like a catastrophic availability collapse. It is not. Token-matching dead SKUs against live ones shows Rs 6,68,720 (68%) is grammage/SKU-code churn — "Cadbury Dairy Milk Fruit & Nut 36 Gm" is dead while "Cadbury Dairy Milk 36 Gm Fruit & Nut" is the #3 seller at Rs 95,834; same for 12.5g/12.1g, 23g/21g, "Silk Oreo"/"Silk Oreo 58.5 Gm", "36G Crackle"/"Crackle 36 Gm".

THIRD: the residual no-twin dead list is dominated by Cream Bell, which reads as a stock-out but is a DISTRIBUTOR SWITCH. Brand-level, prior 12m -> current 12m: Cream Bell Rs 1,27,565 -> Rs 0 (last sale 2025-05-23); Vadilal Rs 1,295 -> Rs 5,42,790; Amul Rs 10,10,690 -> Rs 5,28,759. ARY swapped Cream Bell/Amul for Vadilal. Nothing to recover; it was already recovered.

PRICE LADDER IS COMPLETE (VERIFIED): Rs 1-2 = 135,921 units; Rs 3-5 = 39 SKUs; Rs 6-10 = 64 SKUs / Rs 5.23 L; Rs 11-20 = 42 / Rs 5.36 L; Rs 21-50 = 142 / Rs 15.09 L; Rs 51-100 = 47; Rs 100+ = 93. No price-point hole to fill.

blockers: NOT capital. The whole recovery needs roughly Rs 1.5-2 lakh of working capital against a Rs 7.67 Cr business — the constraint is reorder discipline, not money.
NOT shelf. 861 dead SKUs already occupy the listing; there is no space argument for refusing to keep 53 proven ones in stock.
NOT licence. ARY already retails food; confectionery needs no additional permission.

REORDER CADENCE IS THE REAL BLOCKER: 278 of 431 selling SKUs sit at zero-or-negative on-hand today and only 6 SKUs of 431 sold in all 12 months. Nothing in FusionERP8 is triggering a reorder on a fast-mover going to zero — ProductMaster.QuantityOnHand is dead on 21,471 of 21,472 SKUs, so any reorder report built on that field silently sees nothing. Fix the trigger before touching the range.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP is real and already bit once: the entire Cream Bell range went to zero after 2025-05-23 and had to be replaced by Vadilal. A single-distributor line can vanish without warning; the chocolate recovery leans heavily on one Mondelez route.

HEAT/BLOOM ON THE CHANDIGARH-NAHAN-RAJGARH LEG Apr-Jun caps how hard the solid-bar restock can be pushed in summer — the demand research flags it as the top quality complaint. Panned/sugar-shelled formats (Gems) and wafer bars tolerate the leg better; Silk is the first to show damage.
COLD CHAIN limits the two genuinely absent lines: ice cream cakes need -18C display and pre-order handling, which is why the 4 birthday-cake SKUs have been dead since 2024. Do not chase them.

SEASONALITY IS NOT A BLOCKER BUT MUST NOT BE MISREAD AS ONE: Jan-Feb confectionery collapses to Rs 1.21-2.12 L from a ~Rs 3.5 L baseline in both years (campus vacation, inferred). Ice cream is summer, gazzak is winter. A naive 12-month availability target would over-order both.
